questions.question: Which poet composed the Allahabad Prashasti of Samudragupta?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Harisena**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Allahabad Prashasti (also known as the Prayag Prashasti) was composed by **Harisena**, a court poet and minister of Samudragupta.
 
• Harisena served as the **Mahadandanayaka** (Chief Judicial Officer) and **Sandhivigrahika** (Minister of Peace and War) under Samudragupta.
 
• The Prashasti is inscribed on an **Ashokan pillar** located in Allahabad (Prayagraj).
 
• This inscription provides a detailed account of Samudragupta's conquests, achievements, and patronage of art and culture.
 
• It is written in **Sanskrit** and is considered a classic example of eulogy in Indian inscriptions.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Samudragupta**:

 
 
• Samudragupta (c. 335–380 CE) was one of the greatest rulers of the Gupta Empire.
 
• He is often referred to as the "Napoleon of India" due to his military conquests and expansion of the empire.
 
• He was a patron of art, music, and literature, and his reign marked the beginning of the classical age in Indian history.
 
 
 
• **Prashasti:**
 
 
• A Prashasti is an inscription written in praise of a ruler or a patron, often highlighting their achievements and virtues.
 
• The term "Prashasti" means "praise" in Sanskrit.
 
 
 
• **Ashokan Pillars:**
 
 
• The Allahabad pillar is one of the many pillars erected by Emperor Ashoka during his reign in the 3rd century BCE.
 
• These pillars were later reused by subsequent rulers for inscriptions, such as Samudragupta's Allahabad Prashasti.
 
 
 
• **Gupta Empire:**
 
 
• The Gupta Empire (c. 319–550 CE) is often referred to as the "Golden Age" of India due to its advancements in science, art, and culture.
 
• It witnessed significant achievements in fields such as mathematics, astronomy, literature, and architecture.

questions.question: Which dynasty ruled India between 320 AD and 550 AD?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is the __**Gupta Dynasty**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• The Gupta Dynasty ruled India between 320 AD and 550 AD.
 
• The Gupta empire was founded by Sri Gupta. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• The Gupta Empire rose in Magadha around the 4th century AD and covered the greater part of Northern India.
 
• The Gupta Period is popularly known as the ‘Golden Age of India’.
 
• There is very little information about the first two rulers of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• The important rulers of the Gupta dynasty were:
 
 
• Chandragupta I - (320 - 330 A.D.)
 
• Samudragupta - (330 - 380 A.D.)
 
• Chandragupta II - (380 - 415 A.D.)
 
• Kumaragupta - (415 - 455 A.D.)

questions.question: Who among the following Gupta rulers launched the Nalanda University?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumaragupta.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Kumaragupta,** the son of Chandragupta II, is credited with launching the **Nalanda University** during his reign in the **Gupta Empire.**
 
• The university was a major center of **learning and attracted scholars** from all over the world, including **China, Korea, and Tibet.**
 
• Nalanda University had a **vast library with thousands of books **on various subjects such as **astronomy, mathematics, medicine, and philosophy.** 
 
• The university was destroyed by the **Turkish invader Bakhtiyar Khilji **in the **12th century**, and its ruins were rediscovered in the 19th century. 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Chandragupta II**, also known as Vikramaditya, was a famous Gupta king who is known for his patronage of the** arts and his military campaigns.**
 
• **Skandagupta **was his **successor **who faced invasions from the Huns.
 
• **Vishnugupta **is not a known Gupta ruler.

questions.question: Which of the following titles was held by Samudragupta, a ruler of the Gupta Dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kaviraja**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **Samudragupta **was the **second emperor **of the **Gupta Empire **of **ancient India **and is **regarded among **the **greatest rulers of the dynasty**.
 
• **As a son **of the **Gupta emperor Chandragupta I **and the **Licchavi princess Kumaradevi**, he greatly **expanded **his **dynasty's political **and **military power**.
 
• **Samudragupta **was the **first significant ruler **of the **Gupta Dynasty**.
 
• **Samudragupta **was **not power-hungry**. But **like Napoleon**, he was **never defeated nor sent to exile or jailed**.
 
• **Gupta King Samudragupta **loved to **play the Indian lute **and **love poems**. He not **only penned many poems himself **but also **patronized the poets**. Due to these, he **was titled Kaviraj or King of Poets**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Jahanpanah **was a **fortified city built by Muhammad bin Tughlaq **to **combat the Mongol attacks**. The city has now been ruined but still, people can find walls and a few structures built inside the fort. Jahanpanah means Refuge of the world.
 
• **This imperial title means **"**The Lord **of the **Auspicious Conjunction **in **Persianized Arabic **and **refers to a ruler **whose horoscope **features particular conjunction of Jupiter and Saturn**, **portending a reign of world conquest and justice**.
 
• **Kumargupta **was the **successor of Chandragupta II **and he assumed the title **"Mahendraditya". **He **expanded **the **empire further by **acquiring **provinces **of **Western India**. He **enjoyed a reign **of about **forty years from 414 AD to 455 AD**.

questions.question: Chandragupta, was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** maharaj-adhiraja.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **"Maharaj-adhiraja" **means "**king of kings"** or **"emperor"**, which was a **grand title **adopted by **Chandragupta, **the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty.
 
• Option 1, **"dharamraja**", means **"king of dharma"** or "**king of righteousness"**, which was a title used by some Indian rulers, but not by Chandragupta.
 
• Option 3, **"maharaja"**, means **"king" or "great king",** which was a common title for Indian rulers, but not as grand as "maharaj-adhiraja".
 
• Option 4, "**devanampriya",** means **"beloved of the gods"**, which was a title used by Emperor Ashoka, but not by Chandragupta.
 
• Hence, the statement is **correct **that Chandragupta was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of** "maharaj-adhiraja".**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• From the beginning of the** fourth century CE** to the beginning of the **sixth century CE**, the **Gupta Empire **ruled over ancient India.
 
• The Gupta empire was **started** by** Chandra Gupta I**, the first monarch of India.
 
• The **final **of the great Gupta emperors is typically regarded as **Skandagupta**, the son and successor of Kumaragupta I.

questions.question: Who among the following Gupta kings founded the Nalanda University?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Kumaragupta I.**__ [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta II, also known as **Vikramaditya,** was a famous **Gupta king** who ruled from** 375 to 415 CE**.

 
 
• He was known for his **military conquests** and **patronage of the arts,** but there is no evidence that he founded Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• Chandragupta I was the** founder of the Gupta dynasty** and ruled from **320 to 335 CE**.
 
 
• He was known for his **military campaigns** and **administrative reforms**, but he lived before the establishment of Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• Kumaragupta I was a Gupta king who ruled from **415 to 455 CE.**
 
 
• He was a patron of the** arts and literature.**
 
• He is credited with founding **Nalanda University.**
 
 
 
• Skandagupta was a **Gupta king** who ruled from **455 to 467 CE**.
 
 
• He was known for his **military campaigns** against the Huns, but there is no evidence that he founded Nalanda University.
 
 
 
• Hence, the correct answer is **Option 3 (Kumaragupta I).**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• **Nalanda University** was founded in the **5th century CE **in present-day **Bihar, India.**
 
• It was one of the **oldest and most prestigious centers **of learning in ancient India, attracting **students and scholars** from all over the world.
 
• The university was supported by **various Gupta kings,** who were known for their patronage of** art, literature, and education.**

questions.question: Harishena was a court poet of ______.
questions.solution:
The correct answer is **__Samudragupta__**.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Harishena was a 4th-century Sanskrit poet, panegyrist, and government minister. 
 
• He was an important figure in the court of the **Samudragupta**.
 
• The ‘Prayag Prashasti’ was composed by Harishena.
 
 
• The ‘Prayag Prashasti’ is also known as the Allahabad Pillar Inscription.
 
• It is a pillar inscription of Samudragupta found at Allahabad and written in Sanskrit.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
 

 **Bindusara**
 
 
 
• Bindusara was the son of Chandragupta Maurya, the founder of the Maurya dynasty and ruled from 298 BC to 272 BC. He is also referred to as Amitraghata in Sanskrit Literature. He had two sons Sumana & Ashoka. Ashoka later succeeded him, after his death.
 
 
 
 

 **Bimbisara**
 
 
 
• Bimbisara came from the Haryanka dynasty and ruled for 52 years.
 
• Bimbisara was imprisoned by his son Ajatshatru who ruled the Magadha empire from 492- 460 B.C. He murdered his father Bimbisara.
 
 
 
 

 **Ashoka**
 
 
 
• Ashoka was the son of Bindusara. 
 
• He was governor of Taxila and Ujjain during his father’s reign. 
 
• Ashoka sat on the throne around 268 B.C after successfully defeating his brothers.

questions.question: Who among the following was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the grand title of Maharaj-adhiraja?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta I**__.

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta I was the first ruler of the Gupta dynasty to adopt the title of Maharajadhiraja__.
 
• Chandragupta I was a son of the Gupta king Ghatotkacha, and a grandson of the dynasty's founder Gupta, both of whom are called Maharaja in the Allahabad Pillar inscription.
 
• He was also the father of Samudragupta, his next successor.</

questions.question: After the victory over Sakas, who among the following adopted the title of 'Vikramaditya'?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is __**Chandragupta II.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• Chandragupta II:-

 
 
• One of the most powerful emperors of the Gupta dynasty was Chandragupta II, also known by his given name Vikramaditya and Chandragupta Vikramaditya. **(Hence option 4 is correct)**
 
• He was the third ruler of the Gupta Empire in India.
 
• The famous Chandragupta II was the child of Samudragupta and Datta Devi.
 
• The Gupta empire was extended by Chandragupta II to the western sea coast, a vital area for trade and commerce.
 
• As a result, Malwa and Ujjain (Ujjayini), the region's capital, enjoyed prosperity.
 
• The second capital of Chandragupta II was Ujjayini.
 
 

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Chandragupta I (319AD-334 AD):

 
 
• He was the first Gupta ruler to assume the title of *Maharajadhiraja*.
 
• He strengthened his kingdom by the matrimonial alliance with the powerful family of Lichchhavis, who were the rulers of Mithila.
 
• He got married to the Lichchhavi princess *Kumaradevi*.
 
• He started the Gupta Era in 319AD-320 AD.
 
• He established his authority over Magadha, Saketa and Prayaga.
 
 
 
• **Skandagupta:-**
 
 
• Skanda Gupta also took the title Vikramaditya.
 
• Skandagupta was the last powerful Gupta Monarch.
 
• He took the title of Maharajadhiraja.
 
• Bhitari pillar depicts the information about Skandagupta of the Gupta Empire.
 
 
 
• Kumaragupta I:-
 
 
• ​He was the son and successor of Chandragupta II.
 
• Kumaragupta I's reign was marked by peace and relative inactivity, which was a result of the stability and prosperity achieved during the reign of his father, Chandragupta II.

questions.question: Which of the following universities was founded by Kumaragupta, the ruler of the Gupta dynasty?
questions.solution:
The correct answer is__** Nalanda University.**__

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/36f36cd5ece4186095afcf2ffbfb7b80cc04b6c2e3226e7477a419a9fbc96f85.png] **__Key Points__**

__
 
• **The university of Nalanda** was famous and one of the most prestigious during the 5th century onwards.
 
• The University of Nalanda was set up by** Kumar Gupta**, one of the famous rulers of the Gupta Dynasty.
 
• Nalanda University was devoted to not only Buddhist studies but also trained students in fine arts, medicine, mathematics, astronomy, politics, and the art of war.
 
• There were also other India's early universities and learning centers such as **Taxila, Nalanda, and Vikramashila**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **Additional Information__**

 
• Delhi University was founded in **1922 by an Act of the Central Legislative Assembly.**
 
• Pune University was established in **1949 **and is spread over a 411-acre (1.66 km2) campus in the neighborhood of Ganeshkhind.
 
• The University of ancient Taxila was an ancient university located in the city of Taxila (in modern-day Pakistan) near the bank of the Indus River.
 
• Nalanda University is known as the first university in India. The university was established in the 5th century and lasted till the 13th century.
